area: transients-dispatch: conj!/assoc!/instance? through cohost.shim/dot, check-cast and the jolt adapter. jolt internals were read at tag v0.8.23, the installed binary (/root/.jolt/aot-cache/v0.8.23-…), with `git show v0.8.23:…` in /root/.cache/vs-hosts/jolt. That checkout's HEAD (dc8fd57) is newer, and v0.8.23 has no class-name memo. The JVM bench file target/bench-clj.edn is used as a control.

findings.claim: The slowdown is not the transient, reduce or range. It is the instance-method interop path. core.clj's conj and assoc call RT statics, which the codemod turns into shim vars bound to the host's own fns. conj!/assoc! call .conj/.assoc on locals hinted ^ITransient*, which become ((cohost.shim/dot "conj" cohost.shim/-conj) (cohost.shim/check-cast 'clojure.lang.ITransientCollection coll) x). conj-vector and transient-vector use the same harness: stock reduce, then host reduce over the host range, with one stock fn call per element. Stock times are 9.77 vs 610.94 ms per 100k, so (610.94-9.77)/100k = 6.01 µs per element is spent in dot + check-cast + the dispatcher. bench-jolt.edn medians agree: 11.18 vs 613.19 ms, 6.02 µs. The host's own conj! is cheaper than its conj (4.34 vs 9.8 ms), so none of this cost is the transient itself. into-vector (6.13 µs/elem) and set-build (6.62) carry the same per-element cost; their ratios are lower (x56, x35) only because jolt's own into costs 110-190 ns/elem against 43 ns for its bare conj!. The JVM shows the same split where instance?/class/str are native: 3.03 vs 49.85 ms, about 0.47 µs per conj!, x27 vs its own 1.83 ms. So the shim's own work counts on every host, not only jolt's primitives.

findings.claim: instance-of? canonicalizes its constant class token on every call, and canon's has-dot? scans the token's name from the end one char at a time, allocating a 1-char string at each step. Every interface-preds key already contains a dot and is already canonical. The rewriter already emits full names (class-token; checked-hints values). So this work changes nothing. Iterations per call: 21 for clojure.lang.ITransientCollection (conj! check-cast); 22 for ITransientAssociative (assoc!); 8 for java.lang.Integer (transduce's integer?); 12 for IChunkedSeq (the lazy map in frequencies).

findings.claim: jolt answers (instance? ITransientCollection t) for its own transient with an uncached arm walk on every call. A jolt-transient has no instance kind key: class-fast-name lists no transient and ref-kind-key does not cover it. So the call-site cache and the verdict memo never apply, and instance-check-walk runs the registry newest-first until the ITransient arm. In v0.8.23 that is about 17 arms: post-prelude, natives-queue x2, proxy, zip-out, zip-in, io-streams, natives-array, inst-time, nio-file, io x2, byte-buffer, then Class, the class-name arm, map-entry, ITransient. The class-name arm calls jolt-class-name, which in v0.8.23 has no memo, so each call also walks the class arms to the transient's arm. Some arms (ITransient, io-streams, inst-time) cut substrings of the type name. host/transient? runs once per conj! (check-cast). It runs twice per assoc!, because -assoc asks again after check-cast has already proved it. That second walk is consistent with group-by costing 3.07 µs/elem more than transient-vector. Stock mod accounts for only ~0.49 µs (set-build - into-vector).

findings.claim: Every (.m x ...) goes through dot's closure, which asks host-object? and then host/user-type? before it calls the shim fn. On jolt and the JVM, user-type? first renders (str (class x)) and string-tests it, even for receivers that can never be user types. Here those receivers are the host's own transient (conj!/assoc!) and a class-token symbol (every stock instance?). For a jolt transient in v0.8.23, (class x) walks the class arms (no memo). For any receiver, (str cls) goes through jolt-str-one / jolt-str-render-one and the str-render registry, newest-first, to the jclass arm. jclass's arm comes from class-model.ss, loaded early, so the later-registered arms are tried first. The answer is false every time. jolt.clj's invoke-member and its member cache are only reached when user-type? is true, so they are not on any of these paths.

findings.claim: transduce has no transients. Its x50 (3.79 µs/elem vs 77 ns) comes from the same machinery reached through core.clj's instance?, a .isInstance interop call, once per element: odd? calls even?, which calls integer?, which calls (instance? Integer n). Each call allocates dot's closure, runs user-type? on the class-token symbol (finding 4), then -isInstance, then instance-of?, then canon('java.lang.Integer) with 8 has-dot? iterations, then interface-preds, then jolt integer?. The rest of the element is about 10 stock transducer and arithmetic calls (map step, inc, filter step, not, bit-and, uncheckedLongCast, zero?, +). The fn-call and conj-vector cases show stock calls like these cost tens of ns each, not µs. policy.cljc already replaces cast with a direct instance-of? call; instance? is not replaced. The JVM shows the same: transduce stock 31.64 vs host 1.14 ms, x28.

findings.claim: assoc! costs more than conj!. It runs check-cast with 22 has-dot? iterations, the host/transient? walk twice (check-cast, then -assoc again), user-type? on the transient map, and a 3-arg dispatcher. The per-element body also adds stock mod (rem, zero?, =, pos? x2), get and conj. group-by measures 9.18 µs/elem against transient-vector's 6.11; set-build - into-vector puts stock mod at ~0.49 µs. frequencies (13.66 µs/elem) also reduces over a stock lazy (map f (range n)). jolt's range seq is not the shim's ChunkedCons, so stock map takes the unchunked branch. Every element then calls chunked-seq?, a stock instance? that dispatches again (finding 4, canon 12 iterations), and allocates a LazySeq and a cons. That accounts for frequencies - group-by = 4.48 µs/elem; the lazy part belongs to the lazy-pipeline area.

probes.tests: P0, the harness floor: a stock fn called per element by host reduce over a host range. Subtract it from P3-P11. If it is not far below conj-vector's ~10 ms, the per-element harness is not negligible and the deltas below must be read against it.

P2, the same as the case but calling the host's conj! through the shim var, with no dot and no check-cast. Confirms finding 1 if near jolt's own 4-10 ms against the case's ~611 ms. Refutes it (the cost is elsewhere: reduce, range, transient) if this is above ~100 ms.
P3, check-cast alone (canon + interface-preds + host/transient?). Its share of the ~600 ms is P3 - P0. The remainder of (P1 - P2) is dot + the dispatcher.

P4/P13, canon at 21 vs 8 has-dot? iterations. The difference / 1.3M is the per-iteration cost. Confirms finding 2 (fix 1 is a large win) if the first timing is a large part of P3. Refutes it if both are small (under ~50 ms).
P5, cap + jolt's uncached instance-check walk for a transient. A large value confirms finding 3. P3 - P5 is roughly canon's share, a cross-check on P4.

probes.form: (let [tp (:transient? (cohost.adapter/current)) jt (cohost.adapter/var-root (cohost.adapter/resolve-core 'transient?)) t (transient [])] [(time (reduce (fn [a x] (tp t)) nil (range 100000))) (time (reduce (fn [a x] (jt t)) nil (range 100000)))])
probes.tests: P6, the adapter's (instance? ITransientCollection t) walk vs jolt's native transient? record test, without cap. The difference is fix 2's saving per call: 1 per conj!, 2 per assoc!. Refutes finding 3 if the two are close.

P7, user-type? + cap on a jolt transient (class-arm walk + str render) and on a class-token symbol (fast class path + str render). These are fixes 2 and 3's savings per dispatch. Refutes finding 4 if both are small next to P1 - P2.
P8, dot's per-call closure allocation and set lookup, and one bare cap. If both are near P0, finding 5 is minor and fixing dot (hoisting) is not worth a rewriter change.

probes.form: [(time (reduce (fn [a x] (instance? Integer x)) nil (range 100000))) (time (reduce (fn [a x] (cohost.shim/instance-of? 'java.lang.Integer x)) nil (range 100000)))]
probes.tests: P9, transduce's per-element unit. The first is the stock instance? (dot + dispatcher + instance-of?); the second the shim predicate directly. The difference is fix 4's saving. Confirms finding 6 if the first is most of transduce's 379 ms, i.e. 2-3+ s per 1M rescaled to 100k ~ hundreds of ms. Refutes it if well under 100 ms (then the arithmetic shims dominate transduce).

probes.form: (let [f (fn [m i] (assoc! m (rem i 31) i)) g (fn [m i] (cohost.shim/-assoc m (rem i 31) i))] [(time (count (persistent! (reduce f (transient {}) (range 100000))))) (time (count (persistent! (reduce g (transient {}) (range 100000)))))])
probes.tests: P10, the assoc! dispatch (frequencies/group-by) against -assoc alone, which still pays one host/transient?. The difference is check-cast(22) + dot + user-type?. Compare with P1 - P2 to test finding 7's claim that assoc! costs more than conj!.

P11, the per-element dispatch the stock lazy map adds in frequencies (chunked-seq? is a stock instance? with canon 12). Confirms finding 7's frequencies - group-by attribution if close to ~300+ ms per 100k (about 3 µs each).
